identity.title: Binding of SARS-CoV-1/2 NSP1 to DNA Polymerase alpha-Primase Inhibits DNA Replication through Reduction of Interaction between DNA and DNA Polymerase alpha-Primase.

content.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the atomic level mechanism governing the binding nonstructural protein 1 of SARS-CoV-1 (SARS-CoV-1 NSP1) and SARS-CoV-2 (SARS-CoV-2 NSP1) to Pol alpha-primase is important to advance the development of small molecule inhibitors for the treatment COVID-19. In this study, we use both all-atom steered molecular dynamics (all-atom SMD) and coarse-grained umbrella sampling (coarse-grained US) simulations to assess the binding affinity of SARS-CoV-1 NSP1 and SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 to Pol alpha-primase. Our all-atom SMD and coarse-grained US simulations consistently indicate that SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 exhibits stronger affinity for Pol alpha-primase compared to SARS-CoV-1 NSP1, implying that SARS-CoV-2 poses a greater risk than SARS-CoV-1 in impeding DNA replication for DNA synthesis. Through an energetic decomposition analysis of the interaction energies within these complexes, we identify electrostatic interactions as the primary contributors to the observed difference in binding affinity. We found that hydrogen bonds between Asp33 and Arg616 in SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase, and Asp33 with Arg616 and Lys655 in SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase, are critical for the interaction of both SARS-CoV-1 NSP1 and SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 with Pol alpha-primase. Asp33 in SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 shows increased solubility and stability compared to SARS-CoV-1 NSP1, enhancing its association with Pol alpha-primase. This finding lays the groundwork for innovative strategies aimed at inhibiting the interaction between these entities, offering promising avenues for therapeutic intervention against COVID-19. We also estimated the binding free energy of DNA to Pol alpha-primase, SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase, and SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase using the MM-PBSA method. The results show the order: Pol alpha-primase-DNA < SARS1 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase-DNA < SARS2 NSP1-Pol alpha-primase-DNA, indicating that both SARS-CoV-1 NSP1 and SARS-CoV-2 NSP1 reduce DNA binding to Pol alpha-primase, suggesting impaired DNA synthesis.
